questions.question: How is a classic repo typically treated on the cash borrower's balance sheet under IFRS?
options: The securities remain on balance sheet and a secured liability is recognised in addition
The securities are derecognised and a gain on sale is booked
The transaction appears only off balance sheet as a contingent liability
Only the net interest expense is recognised, with no balance sheet impact
questions.explanation: Because substantially all risks and rewards stay with the seller, there is no derecognition. The repo is shown as secured financing — which inflates the balance sheet and matters for the leverage ratio and reporting dates.

questions.question: What is a repurchase agreement (repo) in its basic form?
options: A sale of securities combined with a simultaneous agreement to repurchase them at a later date at a pre-agreed price
An unsecured interbank loan with a maturity of up to one year
A forward contract on an interest rate with no exchange of securities
A permanent transfer of securities against a periodic lending fee
questions.explanation: A repo has two linked legs: the sale (near leg) and the agreed repurchase (far leg) of the same or equivalent securities at a fixed price. The price difference is economically the interest.

questions.question: What is the same transaction called from the perspective of the party that provides cash and receives securities?
options: A reverse repo
A sell/buy-back
A short repo
A collateral swap
questions.explanation: Repo and reverse repo are two views of one transaction. Giving cash and taking collateral is a reverse repo; taking cash and delivering collateral is a repo.

questions.question: In SIX Repo terminology, the cash borrower is also referred to as the:
options: Collateral seller
Collateral buyer
Cash lender
Aggressor
questions.explanation: SIX Repo defines cash borrower = collateral seller (borrows cash, sells collateral) and cash lender = collateral buyer (lends cash, buys collateral).

questions.question: Which statement about the motivation for repo trading is correct?
options: Repos can be cash-driven (funding or investing cash) or securities-driven (obtaining a specific security)
Repos serve only short-term funding purposes
Repos serve only to obtain securities to cover short positions
Repos are primarily a tool for managing foreign exchange risk
questions.explanation: Cash-driven: the borrower needs liquidity and delivers GC. Securities-driven: the cash lender wants a specific bond (a special) and accepts a lower repo rate for it.

questions.question: How are the two settlement dates of a repo commonly referred to?
options: Purchase date (near leg) and repurchase date (far leg)
Opening trade and closing auction
Spot leg and option leg
Primary settlement and secondary settlement
questions.explanation: On the purchase date cash moves against securities; on the repurchase date the transaction is unwound at the repurchase price.

questions.question: What does the term 'repo rate' refer to?
options: The annualised rate of return on the cash amount, expressed via the difference between purchase and repurchase price
The percentage discount applied to the market value of the collateral
The fee charged by the triparty agent
The yield of the security delivered as collateral
questions.explanation: The repo rate is the price of the money, not of the paper. The discount on the collateral is the haircut (or margin ratio).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a classic repo?
options: The seller gives up all economic exposure to the security
Legal title to the securities passes to the buyer
The repurchase price is fixed when the trade is struck
The seller keeps the market risk of the collateral
questions.explanation: A repo transfers legal title but not economic exposure: price moves on the collateral stay with the seller, who takes the security back at a price fixed at the outset. That combination is what makes a repo a secured loan rather than a sale.

questions.question: A corporate treasury invests CHF 50 million for one week against government bonds. Which side of the repo is it on?
options: The reverse repo side — cash lender and collateral buyer
The repo side — cash borrower and collateral seller
Neither; this is a securities lending trade
It depends on whether the bonds are Swiss
questions.explanation: Whoever puts cash out and takes securities in is doing a reverse repo. The label follows the direction of the cash, not the type of the collateral or the identity of the parties.

questions.question: In a repo, what exactly is the 'collateral'?
options: The securities sold to the cash lender on the purchase date and bought back on the repurchase date
The cash amount advanced by the lender
A guarantee issued by a third party such as a CCP
The margin held by the triparty agent as a fee reserve
questions.explanation: Collateral is the asset that secures the exposure. In repo it is the securities themselves, transferred outright rather than pledged, which is why the cash lender can sell them immediately if the borrower defaults.

questions.question: What is the near leg of a repo?
options: The opening settlement on the purchase date: cash to the borrower, collateral to the lender
The final settlement, when the collateral is returned
The point at which the repo rate is fixed
The daily margin exchange
questions.explanation: The near leg starts the trade on the purchase date. The nearer of the two settlement dates gives it its name.

questions.question: What is the far leg of a repo?
options: The closing settlement on the repurchase date: collateral back to the seller, repurchase price back to the lender
The opening exchange of cash against securities
The substitution of one security for another
The moment a margin call is settled
questions.explanation: The far leg unwinds the trade at the repurchase price, which is the original cash amount plus accrued repo interest. A failure on the far leg is particularly awkward: the borrower has paid but has not received its collateral back.

questions.question: What is meant by the 'counterparty' to a repo trade?
options: The other party to the contract, which owes and is owed obligations under it
The agent that allocates the collateral
The venue on which the trade was executed
The issuer of the security used as collateral
questions.explanation: Every bilateral trade has exactly two counterparties. Where a CCP is involved it becomes the counterparty to both original parties through novation, which is why counterparty exposure then sits with the CCP.

questions.question: What is counterparty risk in a repo?
options: The risk that the other party fails to perform, leaving a shortfall once the collateral has been realised
The risk that the collateral price falls during the trade
The risk of sending a wrong settlement instruction
The risk that the repo rate moves against you
questions.explanation: Collateral does not remove counterparty risk, it caps it. What remains is the gap between the claim and what the collateral actually fetches — which is why haircuts, daily margining and a short margin period of risk matter.

questions.question: What is a collateral swap (collateral upgrade trade)?
options: A transaction exchanging securities against securities of a different quality, with no cash leg
A repo in which the cash currency is changed during the life of the trade
The replacement of delivered collateral by equivalent collateral during the trade
An interest rate swap referencing the repo rate
questions.explanation: In a collateral swap a party exchanges, say, equities for government bonds (an upgrade) to meet LCR requirements. Replacing collateral with equivalent collateral during a trade is instead a substitution.

questions.question: On a trading platform such as CO:RE, who is the 'aggressor' in a trade?
options: The participant who responds to a quote or request for offer and thereby creates the trade
The participant who posts the quote or request for offer
The participant with the larger cash amount
The participant who delivers the collateral
questions.explanation: The responder is the aggressor, the poster is the non-aggressor. For trades resulting directly from an order, both counterparties count as aggressors — and the distinction affects the transaction fee charged.

questions.question: What distinguishes an 'order' from a 'quote' on CO:RE?
options: An order is a binding offer sent to a selected participant, whereas a quote is generally non-binding
An order is non-binding and a quote is binding
Orders are only used by the SNB, quotes only by banks
Orders are always multilateral, quotes always bilateral
questions.explanation: Orders are binding and used to initiate trading directly with a specific counterparty or to respond to a quote or RfO. Quotes and requests for offer are generally non-binding invitations.

questions.question: What does the auto-hit function on a trading desk do?
options: It causes an order sent in response to a quote to be accepted automatically, within configured limits
It automatically increases the cash amount of a trade
It automatically rolls the repurchase date every day
It automatically substitutes collateral when the value falls
questions.explanation: Auto-hit limits are configured at trading desk level and can be modified by any trader. They speed up execution for standard sizes without manual confirmation.

questions.question: Who economically benefits from a coupon paid on the collateral during the life of a repo?
options: The collateral giver (seller) — the buyer passes the amount on as a manufactured payment
The buyer, since they are the legal owner and keep the coupon
Both parties split it equally
The triparty agent, which retains it to cover fees
questions.explanation: The buyer receives the coupon technically but must pass it on as a manufactured payment. Economically the security stays with the collateral giver.

questions.question: Who bears the market risk of the collateral during the life of a repo?
options: The collateral giver (seller), because they take the securities back at the far leg
The buyer, because they are the legal owner
The triparty agent
Nobody — the fixed repurchase price neutralises it
questions.explanation: The repurchase price is fixed and independent of the collateral's price path. Gains and losses stay with the seller; the buyer protects itself against value loss through haircut and margining.

questions.question: What is a bond?
options: A debt instrument under which the issuer owes the holder defined interest payments and repayment of principal at maturity
A share in the ownership and profits of a company
A contract to exchange interest payments on a notional amount
A short-term deposit with a bank
questions.explanation: A bondholder is a creditor, not an owner. That is why bonds rank ahead of equity in insolvency and why they are the natural collateral for secured funding.

questions.question: Why is a bond described as a fixed-income asset?
options: Because its payment schedule is contractually defined rather than discretionary
Because its market price never changes
Because its yield is guaranteed by the state
Because it can only be issued at a fixed rate of interest
questions.explanation: 'Fixed income' refers to the contractual nature of the cash flows, not to a fixed price or even a fixed coupon — floating rate notes are fixed income too. Prices still move with rates and credit spreads.

questions.question: What is the fixed-income market?
options: The market in which debt instruments — bonds and money market paper — are issued and traded
The market for equities with stable dividends
The market for interest rate derivatives only
The market in which central banks set policy rates
questions.explanation: The repo market sits alongside it as the funding layer: fixed-income positions are largely financed in repo, so the two markets are operationally inseparable.

questions.question: What is an ISIN?
options: A twelve-character code that uniquely identifies a specific security internationally
A code identifying the legal entity issuing a security
A reference number assigned to an individual trade
An identifier for a settlement account at a CSD
questions.explanation: ISIN answers 'which security'. The entity is identified by an LEI and the individual transaction by a UTI — three different identifiers that reporting systems constantly have to keep apart.

questions.question: How is a repo best characterised economically?
options: As a collateralised loan
As a purchase with a right of return and no interest component
As a derivative with a daily cash settlement obligation
As a pure securities transaction without any credit component
questions.explanation: Legally it is a sale with a repurchase (title transfer), but economically it is a secured loan: cash against collateral, remunerated at the repo rate.

questions.question: Why is the repo rate typically below the unsecured money-market rate for the same maturity?
options: Because the transaction is collateralised and therefore carries materially lower credit risk
Because repos receive preferential tax treatment
Because repos are always transacted with the central bank
Because repos may not have a maturity longer than one day
questions.explanation: Collateral substantially reduces loss given default, so a lower risk premium is demanded than in the unsecured market.

questions.question: What happens to legal ownership of the securities during the life of a classic repo?
options: Full title passes to the buyer (title transfer)
Title stays with the seller and the buyer only obtains a pledge
Title is transferred to a neutral trustee
Title is suspended and attributed to neither party until the far leg
questions.explanation: The classic repo (GMRA) rests on title transfer: the buyer becomes full legal owner and may re-use the securities. This is exactly what makes close-out so fast in a default — no pledge enforcement proceedings are needed.

questions.question: What happens to the collateral if the cash borrower defaults during the life of the trade?
options: The cash lender can liquidate the collateral and net the proceeds against its claim (close-out netting)
The collateral falls into the insolvency estate and the cash lender becomes an ordinary creditor
The collateral automatically transfers to the central bank
The trade is unwound at the original purchase price
questions.explanation: Thanks to title transfer and close-out netting provisions in the master agreement, the cash lender can realise the collateral immediately and settle all positions at a single net amount.

questions.question: Why does a repo transfer credit risk differently than an unsecured deposit?
options: Exposure is reduced to the residual gap between the claim and the liquidation value of the collateral
Credit risk is fully eliminated in every case
Credit risk shifts entirely to the triparty agent
Credit risk becomes market risk on the cash amount
questions.explanation: Collateral converts most of the credit exposure into market and liquidity risk on the securities. What remains is gap risk: the possibility that the collateral loses more value than the haircut covers before it can be sold.

questions.question: Which day-count convention is market standard for CHF and EUR repo interest?
options: ACT/360
ACT/365
ACT/ACT
questions.explanation: CHF and EUR money markets use ACT/360 — the same 'Euro interest calculation method' SIX Repo applies when computing term-adjusted transaction fees. GBP conventionally uses ACT/365.

questions.question: What do 'DVP cut-off days' specify for contract types with a negotiable purchase date?
options: The minimum number of currency business days that must elapse between trade date and purchase date
The latest time of day at which a trade can be agreed
The number of days a margin call may remain unpaid
The number of days before a substitution takes effect
questions.explanation: With one DVP cut-off day and a 13:00 purchase date cut-off time, the earliest purchase date is T+1 and the trade must be struck by 13:00. Trading later may still be possible if the purchase date is beyond T+1.

questions.question: What does the 'end-to-end convention' mean for monthly contract types (1M–12M)?
options: Purchase and repurchase dates use the same day of the month, unless the purchase date is the last currency business day of the month, in which case the repurchase date is also the month end
Every trade ends on the last calendar day of the month
The repurchase date is always exactly 30 days later
The repurchase date is set by the triparty agent at month end
questions.explanation: So 3 January runs to 3 June, but 31 January runs to 28 February. Without this rule, month-end trades would drift into the next month.

questions.question: What does the 'following modified' day roll convention do when a repurchase date falls on a currency holiday?
options: It rolls the date forward to the next currency business day, unless that falls into the next month, in which case it rolls back to the previous business day
It always rolls the date forward, even into the next month
It always rolls the date backwards
It cancels the trade
questions.explanation: The 'modified' part prevents a trade from slipping into the following month, which would distort month-end funding and accrual periods.

questions.question: What is a haircut in a repo?
options: A percentage deduction from the collateral's market value, so less cash is advanced than the collateral is worth
A fee deducted from the repo interest
A reduction of the repo rate for high quality collateral
A discount granted to frequent counterparties
questions.explanation: The haircut is the cash lender's cushion. It absorbs the price fall that could occur between a default and the sale of the collateral — nothing to do with the price of the money, which is the repo rate.

questions.question: What does 'margin' refer to in secured financing?
options: The excess of collateral value over the cash exposure, and the transfers that maintain it
The profit a desk makes on a trade
The difference between the bid and the offer
The fee paid to the trading venue
questions.explanation: Margin is protection, not profit. It is established at the outset as initial margin or a haircut, and maintained over the life of the trade through variation margin transfers.

questions.question: What is the difference between the clean price and the dirty price of a bond?
options: The dirty price includes interest accrued since the last coupon; the clean price excludes it
The dirty price includes the haircut; the clean price does not
The clean price is the mid, the dirty price is the offer
The dirty price is the price after settlement costs
questions.explanation: Bonds are usually quoted clean but settled dirty. Collateral must be valued at the dirty price — ignoring accrued interest leaves the cash lender quietly under-collateralised, and the gap grows as the coupon date approaches.

questions.question: A bond has a market value including accrued interest of CHF 10,000,000 and the haircut is 2%. What is the cash amount?
questions.explanation: Cash = market value × (1 − haircut) = 10m × 0.98 = CHF 9,800,000. The CHF 200,000 of over-collateralisation protects the cash lender.

questions.question: In SIX Repo product terms, what does a margin ratio of 100% (i.e. 1) mean?
options: The value of the collateral provided equals the cash amount — no over-collateralisation
The collateral is worth twice the cash amount
No collateral is required at all
The haircut equals 100%
questions.explanation: The margin ratio is the collateral-to-cash ratio. At 100% the collateral value equals the cash amount; standard CHF bond GC contract types trade at a margin ratio of 1, while equity contract types often use 1.05.

questions.question: Which value of the collateral is used for the collateralisation calculation?
options: The dirty price, i.e. market price plus accrued interest
The clean price excluding accrued interest
The nominal value
The book value in the seller's accounts
questions.explanation: Only the dirty price reflects the true economic value. Ignoring accrued interest leaves the cash lender systematically under-collateralised.

questions.question: What is initial margin in a repo?
options: The over-collateralisation agreed at the outset, expressed as collateral value divided by cash amount
Margin exchanged daily as prices move
A deposit lodged with the trading venue before trading
The minimum size of a trade
questions.explanation: Initial margin and haircut are two ways of saying the same thing: an initial margin of 102% corresponds to a haircut of roughly 1.96%. Margin exchanged as prices move afterwards is variation margin.

questions.question: How is the cash amount derived when a margin ratio of 102% is used instead of a haircut?
options: Cash = collateral value / margin ratio, i.e. 10m / 1.02 = CHF 9,803,922
Cash = collateral value × margin ratio, i.e. CHF 10,200,000
Cash = collateral value minus 2 percentage points, i.e. CHF 9,800,000
Cash = collateral value; the margin is posted separately in cash
questions.explanation: Margin ratio and haircut express the same idea differently: margin ratio = 1/(1 − haircut). A 2% haircut corresponds to a margin ratio of about 102.04%, not exactly 102%.

questions.question: Which factors most strongly drive the size of a haircut?
options: Volatility, liquidity, residual maturity and credit quality of the collateral, plus the term of the repo
Only the credit quality of the counterparty
Only the currency of the cash amount
The level of the repo rate
questions.explanation: The haircut covers the risk that the collateral loses value between default and liquidation. Volatile, illiquid, long-dated or lower-rated paper attracts bigger discounts.

questions.question: What does it mean to mark a repo to market?
options: Revaluing the collateral and the cash exposure at current market prices to see whether margin is due
Adjusting the repo rate to current market rates
Re-registering the collateral in the buyer's name
Reporting the trade to a trade repository
questions.explanation: Marking to market is what turns a static contract into a managed exposure. Without daily revaluation, a collateral shortfall would only surface when it is too late to do anything about it.

questions.question: What is a margin call in a repo context?
options: A demand for additional collateral or cash because the exposure exceeds the agreed threshold
A demand from the broker to close out the position
An adjustment of the repo rate when market rates move
An automatic recall of the collateral by the seller
questions.explanation: After daily mark-to-market the net exposure is determined. If it exceeds the minimum transfer amount, a margin transfer in cash or securities is called under the master agreement.

questions.question: How often is collateral typically valued in a professionally run repo book?
options: At least daily (mark-to-market), and in triparty sometimes intraday
Monthly at month end
Only at inception and at maturity
Quarterly, together with regulatory reporting
questions.explanation: Daily mark-to-market is market standard and a supervisory expectation. Triparty agents revalue and reallocate collateral continuously.

questions.question: What is a minimum transfer amount (MTA)?
options: A threshold below which no margin call is made, to avoid moving trivial amounts
The smallest tradeable nominal size of a repo
The minimum balance a participant must hold at the central bank
The minimum denomination of the collateral
questions.explanation: The MTA reduces operational effort by suppressing negligible movements. It is agreed in the master agreement or the triparty setup.

questions.question: In a bilateral repo, which party can call for margin?
options: Either party — whichever one is under-collateralised after revaluation
Only the cash lender, since it carries the credit risk
Only the cash borrower, since it owns the collateral economically
Neither; the triparty agent decides unilaterally
questions.explanation: Margining is two-directional. If the collateral rises in value the seller is over-collateralised and can call margin back — a point often missed, and a real source of return for a collateral giver that manages it actively.

questions.question: What is the difference between a margin transfer and a repricing under the GMRA?
options: A margin transfer moves additional collateral or cash, whereas a repricing closes and re-establishes the trade with an adjusted cash amount
The two terms describe the same procedure
Margin transfers are only in cash, repricings only in securities
Repricing means adjusting the repo rate to the market
questions.explanation: A margin transfer leaves the original trade untouched and settles the difference separately. Repricing terminates the old trade and re-opens it at a new purchase price — cleaner in the books, more operationally intensive.

questions.question: A repo is agreed at a repo rate of 1.75%. To which amount is that rate applied?
options: The cash amount
The market value of the collateral
The nominal value of the collateral
The repurchase price
questions.explanation: The repo rate prices the money. Applying it to the collateral value is a common beginner's error and would give the wrong interest whenever a haircut applies.

questions.question: How is the repurchase price of a classic repo calculated?
options: Purchase price × (1 + repo rate × days / day-count basis)
Market value of the collateral on the repurchase date less the haircut
Purchase price plus the coupons paid on the collateral
Purchase price × (1 + repo rate), irrespective of the term
questions.explanation: The repurchase price is the cash amount plus accrued repo interest. The market value of the collateral plays no role in it.

questions.question: A repo of CHF 10,000,000 at a repo rate of 1.50% for 30 days on ACT/360. What is the repo interest?
questions.explanation: 10,000,000 × 0.015 × 30/360 = CHF 12,500, so the repurchase price is CHF 10,012,500.

questions.question: What does a negative repo rate mean?
options: The cash lender effectively pays to obtain the security — the repurchase price is below the purchase price
The haircut is negative, so the trade is under-collateralised
The trade is invalid; negative repo rates cannot be traded
The cash borrower must post additional collateral
questions.explanation: Negative rates occur in negative-interest environments or for heavily demanded specials. The cash lender accepts an interest loss because it needs the paper.

questions.question: How does the repo rate of a special compare to the GC rate?
options: It is below the GC rate because demand for that specific security is high
It is above the GC rate because the security is scarce
It always equals the GC rate
It is unrelated to the GC rate and simply tracks the policy rate
questions.explanation: Whoever badly needs a scarce security must concede on the cash rate. The difference between the GC rate and the special rate is the 'specialness'.

questions.question: For a standard fixed-term GC contract type on CO:RE, which terms are actually negotiable between the parties?
options: Only the cash amount and the repo rate
The term, the basket and the margin ratio
The settlement type and the day-count convention
Everything except the trading currency
questions.explanation: Standard fixed-term contract types are fully standardised: term, collateral type, valuation, periodicity and settlement are fixed, leaving only price and size to negotiate. That standardisation is what makes them liquid.

questions.question: For standard fixed-term contract types on CO:RE, when is repo interest paid?
options: Once, at the end, on the repurchase date
Monthly over the life of the trade
Up front on the purchase date
Daily, together with the mark-to-market
questions.explanation: Periodicity is 'at end', with one payment due on the repurchase date. Interest is therefore embedded in the repurchase price.

questions.question: A trade of CHF 100 million for 7 days is charged 0.45 bps p.a. What is the SIX Repo transaction fee (ACT/360)?
questions.explanation: Fee = term-adjusted volume × rate/10,000 = 100,000,000 × 7/360 × 0.45/10,000 = CHF 87.50. Fees are quoted in basis points per annum and are charged to both counterparties.

questions.question: What characterises an 'indexed' (variable) repo rate type on CO:RE?
options: The rate is pegged to a benchmark index such as SARON and refixed at an agreed frequency, optionally with a spread in basis points
The rate is renegotiated bilaterally every morning
The rate follows the collateral's coupon
The rate is set by the triparty agent
questions.explanation: Fixed-rate repos keep one agreed rate; indexed repos move with the referenced index, with the repo rate fixing frequency determining how often the rate resets. An offset can be expressed in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%).

questions.question: What is a collateral basket?
options: A defined set of eligibility criteria determining which securities may be delivered and on what terms
A vault in which a bank physically stores its collateral
A fixed list of specific ISINs allocated to one individual trade
An index measuring the performance of collateral
questions.explanation: A basket describes rules (issuer type, rating, currency, residual maturity, haircuts, concentration limits) rather than individual securities. That is what makes GC trading efficient: you trade the basket, not the ISIN.

questions.question: In a GC repo on CO:RE, may the collateral seller influence which security is delivered out of the basket?
options: Yes — the collateral seller may additionally specify a security from the selected basket for delivery
No — allocation is entirely random
No — only the cash lender may choose
Only if the trade is a special (SPC) contract type
questions.explanation: The basket defines the eligible universe; within it the seller may nominate a specific security. If the collateral itself is the object of the trade, the correct instrument is a special (SPC) contract type instead.

questions.question: What purpose do concentration limits serve in a collateral basket?
options: They cap the share of any single issuer, ISIN or sector in the delivered collateral pool
They cap the number of trades per counterparty
They cap the repo rate
They cap the maturity of individual trades
questions.explanation: Without concentration limits an entire pool could consist of one illiquid issuer, which would be almost impossible to liquidate without a large price concession in a default.

questions.question: Why is a bank generally not allowed to deliver its own shares or own bonds as collateral?
options: Because of wrong-way risk: the value of the collateral and the default of the counterparty are strongly positively correlated
Because own paper cannot technically be settled in a CSD
Because such securities have no ISIN
Because equities are never eligible as collateral
questions.explanation: If the counterparty defaults, precisely its own paper is close to worthless — the collateral fails at the moment it is needed most. Baskets therefore exclude own and group-affiliated issues.

questions.question: What does a basket definition actually specify?
options: The eligibility rules — issuer types, ratings, currencies, maturities, haircuts and concentration limits — and who owns and maintains them
A fixed list of ISINs that never changes
The prices at which each security may be delivered
The counterparties permitted to trade the basket
questions.explanation: Because a basket is a rule set rather than a list, its contents change as securities are issued, downgraded or redeemed. On CO:RE each basket has a named owner — the SNB, the ECB or SIX Repo AG — who defines those rules.

questions.question: Which prices are used for securities in the ROSA GC basket to make settlement work within SIX SIS?
options: Current prices from SIX Financial Information, which must be available in the ordinary settlement process
Prices quoted by the cash lender
The issuer's last redemption price
Prices from the ECB's eligible asset database
questions.explanation: Basket eligibility is not only about ratings: a security must be priceable in the standard SIX SIS process, otherwise it cannot be valued or margined reliably.

questions.question: What is a substitution?
options: The exchange of delivered collateral for other collateral of equal value and credit quality during the life of the trade
The replacement of a counterparty by a CCP
A change of the cash currency during the trade
The replacement of the master agreement by a new one
questions.explanation: The right of substitution (RoS) lets the collateral seller retrieve a security — because it was sold or is needed as a special — without terminating the repo. In triparty this is largely automated.

questions.question: On CO:RE, what do the trade attributes RtR and RoS stand for?
options: Right to Reuse and Right of Substitution
Rate of Return and Rate of Settlement
Repo trade Reference and Reporting of Securities
Return to Requestor and Rollover of Securities
questions.explanation: RtR determines whether the collateral taker may reuse the specified collateral; RoS determines whether the seller may substitute it for collateral of equal value and credit rating. Both are attributes of the contract type.

questions.question: Under what condition may a collateral seller substitute the collateral it has delivered?
options: Only where the contract type or agreement grants a right of substitution, and the replacement must be of equivalent value and credit quality
At any time and without restriction
Only with the prior approval of the supervisory authority
Only on the repurchase date
questions.explanation: On CO:RE the right of substitution (RoS) is an explicit attribute of the contract type — some standard types grant it, others do not, so it is worth checking before assuming a security can be retrieved.

questions.question: What is a recall in securities lending?
options: The lender demands the return of the lent securities before the agreed end date, for instance in order to sell them
The borrower returns collateral it no longer needs
The CSD cancels a settlement instruction
A central bank withdraws eligibility from a security
questions.explanation: Recall risk is why securities lending is not a reliable funding tool: the lender can pull the securities back. The repo equivalent of retrieving a specific security without ending the trade is substitution.

questions.question: What does 're-use' (rehypothecation) of collateral mean?
options: The collateral receiver uses the securities it received in its own onward transactions
Pledging the same security multiple times within one transaction
Reusing an expired master agreement
Buying back one's own collateral in the market
questions.explanation: Re-use raises efficiency (collateral velocity) but lengthens collateral chains and therefore contagion risk. SFTR consequently requires explicit consent and disclosure of the risks of re-use.

questions.question: What does 'collateral velocity' describe?
options: How often the same securities circulate through further transactions via re-use
The speed of settlement in the CSD
A triparty agent's response time to margin calls
The turnover of the trading book
questions.explanation: High collateral velocity means efficient use of scarce collateral, but increases interconnectedness — a core financial stability topic since 2008.

questions.question: What is the role of a triparty agent?
options: It handles selection, valuation, allocation, substitution and margining of collateral on behalf of both parties
It steps between the parties as central counterparty and assumes the credit risk
It provides the trading platform for price discovery
It reports the transaction to the supervisory authority
questions.explanation: The triparty agent is a service provider, not a counterparty. It takes on no credit risk — that is the fundamental difference from a CCP.

questions.question: What does TPA stand for in collateral management?
options: Triparty agent
Trade processing application
Total portfolio allocation
Transaction pricing agreement
questions.explanation: The TPA sits between the two parties operationally but never becomes a party to the trade: it allocates, values, substitutes and reports, while credit risk stays bilateral.

questions.question: What is collateral allocation?
options: Selecting specific securities from available inventory and assigning them to cover a specific exposure
Deciding how much cash to lend against a basket
Distributing margin calls between counterparties
Splitting a trade into settlement tranches
questions.explanation: Allocation is where eligibility rules, concentration limits, haircuts and optimisation logic all meet. In triparty the agent runs it automatically and reallocates as values move.

questions.question: Which settlement type applies to the GC contract types traded in the CH Repo market on CO:RE?
options: Triparty, with straight-through processing provided through the Triparty Repo Service of SIX Securities Services
Bilateral free-of-payment delivery
Central counterparty clearing with novation
Physical delivery outside any CSD
questions.explanation: Settlement and collateral management run through the SIX triparty service, including risk management, collateral allocation and substitution — and all transactions settle delivery versus payment.

questions.question: What is the key advantage of triparty over purely bilateral collateral management?
options: Automated allocation, valuation and substitution materially reduce operational risk and effort
The triparty agent guarantees performance of the trade
No master agreement is needed any more
The trades no longer have to be reported
questions.explanation: Triparty outsources the daily collateral mechanics to a specialist. The master agreement, reporting duties and credit risk remain entirely with the two parties.

questions.question: What happens in triparty when the market value of allocated collateral falls below the required coverage?
options: The agent automatically allocates further eligible collateral from the giver's available inventory
The trade is closed automatically
The cash lender has to post additional cash
Nothing happens until maturity
questions.explanation: Automatic top-up from available inventory is the core of the triparty model. If inventory is insufficient a collateral deficit arises and the giver must feed in more assets.

questions.question: What is the 'long box' in triparty collateral management?
options: The account holding a participant's available securities, from which the agent draws to allocate collateral
The list of trades still awaiting settlement
The account into which margin calls are paid
The record of securities received from counterparties
questions.explanation: If the long box runs dry, automatic allocation stops and a collateral deficit appears — which is why inventory management upstream of the long box is a core treasury task.

questions.question: What is the key operational difference between a bilateral and a triparty repo?
options: In triparty an agent selects, values and substitutes the collateral; bilaterally the two parties do all of it themselves
In triparty the agent guarantees settlement of the trade
Bilateral repos cannot be collateralised with baskets
Triparty repos are always centrally cleared
questions.explanation: The difference is operational, not legal: the contract stays between the two parties, and so does the credit risk. Bilateral gives control over exactly which security moves; triparty gives scale.

questions.question: What is a collateral pool?
options: The aggregate of securities a participant makes available to cover its secured obligations
A joint account shared by several counterparties
The set of securities a CCP holds as its default fund
A basket owned by a central bank
questions.explanation: Pooling matters because it decouples individual trades from individual securities: obligations are covered from the pool as a whole, which is what makes automated allocation and substitution possible.

questions.question: What does 'cheapest-to-deliver' mean in collateral management?
options: Optimising delivery so that the least costly eligible security is always allocated
Delivering the security with the lowest market price in the portfolio
Delivering the security with the shortest residual maturity
Delivering the security with the highest coupon
questions.explanation: Collateral optimisation delivers the cheapest eligible security — accounting for opportunity cost, LCR value and specialness — and keeps high-quality paper free for more valuable uses.

questions.question: Which securities typically qualify as HQLA Level 1 under Basel III?
options: Central bank reserves and very high quality government bonds
Corporate bonds rated BBB
AAA-rated securitisations
Equities from a main index
questions.explanation: Level 1 covers cash, central bank reserves and top-quality sovereign debt with no haircut in the LCR. Corporates and equities fall at best into Level 2A/2B with discounts.

questions.question: On CO:RE, how is the collateral valued for standard fixed-term contract types?
options: At market value on the purchase date
At the nominal value of the security
At a value freely negotiated between the parties
At the previous month's average price
questions.explanation: For standard fixed-term types collateral valuation is defined as market value on the purchase date. Non-standard types allow a negotiable margin ratio but also value at market on the purchase date.

questions.question: Why does a cross-currency repo (cash in CHF, collateral in EUR) attract an additional haircut?
options: Because FX risk between the collateral and cash currency is added to the market price risk
Because settlement takes longer
Because two master agreements are needed
Because central banks generally prohibit such trades
questions.explanation: If the exchange rate moves adversely, the collateral is worth less measured in the cash currency. The FX add-on (often 3–8%) covers that additional risk.

questions.question: Why is haircut procyclicality a financial stability concern?
options: Rising haircuts in stress reduce available liquidity and force fire sales, which depresses prices further
Because haircuts are too high in calm markets and cost revenue
Because haircuts lengthen the balance sheet
Because haircuts push repo rates negative
questions.explanation: The classic feedback loop: stress → higher haircuts → less cash per unit of collateral → deleveraging and fire sales → lower prices → higher haircuts again.

questions.question: Who owns the SNB GC basket and what does it contain?
options: The Swiss National Bank; it contains SNB eligible securities
SIX Repo AG; it contains all SMI equities
The ECB; it contains euro area government bonds
SIX SIS; it contains all securities held in custody
questions.explanation: SNB GC is a bond basket owned by the SNB with SNB eligible securities in CHF, DKK, EUR, GBP, NOK, SEK and USD. Its content follows the SNB's own eligibility list.

questions.question: Which of these is an equity basket available in the CH Repo market?
options: ROS SMI — Repo of SIX Swiss Market Index equities
USTBOND — US treasury bonds
ECB LC3 — ECB liquidity class 3
L2A CHF — HQLA Level 2A in CHF
questions.explanation: Equity baskets include ROS SMI, ROS SPI, ROS CAC, ROS DAX, ROS FTSE, ROS IBEX, ROS MIB, ROS ETF and US EQUITY. The others listed are bond baskets.

questions.question: What does the US EQUITY basket contain?
options: Constituents of the S&P 500 index, denominated in USD
All US-listed equities including small caps
US corporate bonds
American Depositary Receipts only
questions.explanation: CO:RE facilitates US collateral in three distinct baskets: US treasuries (USTBOND), US corporate bonds (USCBOND) and US equities (S&P 500 constituents).

questions.question: How are the L1 and L2A baskets defined on CO:RE?
options: As sub-sets of SNB GC containing securities meeting Basel III HQLA Level 1 and Level 2A requirements respectively
As baskets of Swiss equities in two liquidity tiers
As ECB haircut categories
As baskets restricted to one-year and two-year maturities
questions.explanation: L1 and L2A slice the SNB GC universe by Basel III HQLA quality, and L1 CHF / L2A CHF narrow it further to CHF-denominated securities — very useful for LCR-driven collateral management.

questions.question: What is the minimum rating requirement for securities in the ROSA GC basket?
options: At least BBB− (S&P) and/or Baa3 (Moody's), with an SBI Composite Rating of at least BBB as a supplementary criterion where no such rating exists
At least AA− from two agencies
Investment grade is not required
At least A− from S&P only
questions.explanation: ROSA GC (Repo of SIX General Collateral) is owned by SIX Repo AG and covers HQLA that is not SNB GC eligible as well as non-HQLA securities down to the lowest investment grade notch.

questions.question: Does SIX Repo AG publish the full list of eligible ISINs for the US collateral baskets?
options: No — SIX Repo publishes no ISIN files and sets no further eligibility criteria for these baskets beyond the broad distinctions
Yes, daily via the CO:RE interface
Yes, monthly in the price list
Only to Premium participants
questions.explanation: For the US baskets SIX Repo relies on broad definitions (US treasuries, US corporate bonds, S&P 500 equities) rather than a published ISIN list — participants must understand which paper qualifies as US securities for withholding tax purposes.

questions.question: How are the ECB LC1 to LC5 baskets on CO:RE structured?
options: As sub-sets of ECB eligible securities corresponding to the ECB haircut categories L1A to L1E
As five maturity buckets of euro government bonds
As five rating classes from AAA down to BBB−
As baskets of five different euro area issuers
questions.explanation: The ECB basket covers all ECB eligible securities; the liquidity classes LC1–LC5 map onto the ECB's own haircut categories L1A–L1E.

questions.question: What role does SIX Repo AG play in the Swiss market?
options: It operates the trading platform for the Swiss repo market and for the SNB's monetary policy operations
It is the Swiss central securities depository
It operates the CHF payment system SIC
It is the central counterparty for all Swiss repo trades
questions.explanation: SIX Repo AG provides the trading venue. Custody and settlement sit with SIX SIS and CHF payments with the SIC system — together they form the Swiss Value Chain.

questions.question: What does the platform name CO:RE stand for?
options: Collateral, Repo and Securities trading
Cooperative Repo Exchange
Central Order Routing Engine
Collateralised Refinancing
questions.explanation: CO:RE is SIX Repo's trading platform for repo and secured money market business, and is also used by the SNB for its operations.

questions.question: What is a request for offer (RfO)?
options: A non-binding request sent to selected participants inviting them to offer a price
A binding order that must be executed
A published quote visible to the whole market
An instruction sent to the triparty agent
questions.explanation: RfOs and quotes are both non-binding invitations; an order is the binding instrument. Whether the recipient set is the whole market or a restricted group also determines the fee and whether the data feeds Swiss reference rates.

questions.question: What does a bid/offer spread represent?
options: The gap between the price at which a market maker will buy and the price at which it will sell
The difference between the GC rate and the special rate
The haircut applied to the collateral
The fee charged by the trading venue
questions.explanation: The spread compensates the market maker for holding risk and standing ready to trade in either direction. In repo the two sides are quoted as rates, so the spread is expressed in basis points.

questions.question: What is a two-way quote?
options: A quote showing both a bid and an offer, so the recipient can trade in either direction
A quote sent to exactly two participants
A quote valid for two business days
A quote that must be answered within two minutes
questions.explanation: Being asked for a two-way price without revealing your direction is standard practice: it stops the quoting party from skewing the price against you once it knows which way you want to go.

questions.question: Which benchmark indices are available for variable-rate contracts on CO:RE?
options: SARON and the SNB Policy Rate for CHF, €STR for EUR, SONIA for GBP and TGCR for USD
LIBOR in all major currencies
EURIBOR and the SNB Policy Rate only
Only SARON
questions.explanation: Each index has its own ISIN on the platform. The SNB Policy Rate index is available only in the SNB market segment.

questions.question: How much notice does SIX Repo AG give before adding or removing a contract type?
options: One week
One month
One quarter
No notice is required
questions.explanation: SIX Repo reserves the right to change the contract type catalogue at any time, subject to one week's notice — worth knowing for anyone maintaining static data in a trading system.

questions.question: In a trade resulting from a quote, which party is the non-aggressor?
options: The participant that posted the quote
The participant that responded to it
Both parties are non-aggressors
Whichever party lends the cash
questions.explanation: Posting is passive, responding is aggressive. The distinction is not academic: aggressor and non-aggressor pay different transaction fees, and market making to the whole market is the cheapest execution type.

questions.question: What is an order book?
options: A record of outstanding buy and sell interest in an instrument, ranked by price and time
A ledger of all settled trades
The list of contract types available on a venue
A participant's internal record of its positions
questions.explanation: Worth knowing what CO:RE is not: for the CH Repo market contract types central trading is not allowed, so trading runs through quotes, requests for offer and addressed orders rather than a central anonymous order book.

questions.question: Where do the exchange rates used for calculations on behalf of CO:RE participants come from?
options: SIX Financial Information
The European Central Bank reference rates
Each participant's own rates
Refinitiv fixings only
questions.explanation: Using one pricing source for both securities valuation and FX conversion keeps triparty allocation, margining and fee calculation internally consistent.

questions.question: What does 'intraday' mean for a repo contract type?
options: Purchase and repurchase happen on the same business day, so the liquidity is provided and returned within the day
The repo has a maturity of one night
The repo rate is refixed several times a day
The collateral is revalued more than once a day
questions.explanation: Intraday (IN) contract types bridge timing gaps between payments in the RTGS system. The SNB posts quotes in CHF IN and TIN, and for fee purposes an intraday trade is charged as if it had a one-day term.

questions.question: How are the contract types in the CH Repo market categorised?
options: Standard GC (fixed term, basket), Non Standard GC (variable term, basket) and Special (variable term, single security)
By counterparty type only
By settlement currency only
Into listed and unlisted contract types
questions.explanation: Standard = fixed term with a basket; Non Standard = variable term with a basket; Special (SPC) = variable term with a specific security as collateral.

questions.question: Which combination does NOT exist among CH Repo market contract types?
options: Fixed term with a single security (special) as collateral
Fixed term with a basket as collateral
Variable term with a basket as collateral
Variable term with a single security as collateral
questions.explanation: Specials are only available with a variable term. Fixed-term contract types always use a basket as collateral.

questions.question: How is a contract type uniquely identified on CO:RE?
options: By its trading currency and subcategory, with each contract type carrying its own identifier
By the ISIN of the delivered collateral
By the LEI of the counterparty
By the trade date and cash amount
questions.explanation: Each contract type has its own reference (Settlm. Org. CT Ref.) and is identified by currency plus subcategory — for example CHF ON BOND or EUR SPC SECURITY.

questions.question: What does the term abbreviation 'TN' denote in a CO:RE contract type?
options: Tom/next — purchase date T+1, repurchase the following business day
Term note with a ten-day maturity
Triparty netting
Terminable notice
questions.explanation: Standard short-dated terms are IN (intraday), ON (overnight, PD T+0), TN (tom/next, PD T+1) and SN (spot/next, PD T+2), followed by weekly and monthly terms out to 12M.

questions.question: What does 'terminable on demand' (ToD) mean for a contract type?
options: The contract can be terminated before the agreed repurchase date
The contract automatically renews unless cancelled
The collateral can be recalled at any time
The repo rate can be renegotiated at any time
questions.explanation: If no repurchase date is set — as for OPEN contract types — the contract must be terminable on demand. For intraday types it means repurchase can happen before end of business.

questions.question: What distinguishes an OPEN contract type from a NON STD contract type on CO:RE?
options: OPEN has no defined repurchase date and is terminable on demand, while NON STD has a negotiable repurchase date
OPEN uses a security as collateral, NON STD a basket
OPEN is always fixed-rate, NON STD always variable-rate
OPEN is only available to the SNB
questions.explanation: OPEN types carry an open repurchase date type, are terminable on demand and are typically variable-rate; NON STD types have a negotiable repurchase date and may be fixed or variable rate.

questions.question: Which purchase date (T+X) applies to standard overnight (ON) contract types?
options: T+0 — the purchase date is the trade date
It is freely negotiable
questions.explanation: ON settles same day (T+0), TN settles T+1 and SN as well as the weekly and monthly standard terms settle T+2.

questions.question: What is the Evergreen (EVG) flag on CO:RE?
options: A trade-level flag that rolls the repurchase date forward by one day at end of day, keeping the original term constant
A separate contract type for perpetual repos
A basket containing only green bonds
An automatic rate reset every morning
questions.explanation: EVG is not a contract type but a trade attribute. Once an evergreen trade is called, the daily rolls stop and it continues as a normal fixed-term repo until repurchase.

questions.question: For which terms is the Evergreen flag NOT available?
options: OPEN and INTRADAY terms
1M and 3M terms
Overnight and tom/next terms
Special (SPC) contract types
questions.explanation: EVG may be offered on fixed-term, NON and SPC contract types where marked, but never on OPEN or INTRADAY — rolling a date forward makes no sense where there is no fixed term to preserve.

questions.question: What margin ratio range can be negotiated for non-standard contract types?
options: From 0.0001% up to 999%
Exactly between 100% and 105%
Only 100%
Between 90% and 110%
questions.explanation: Non-standard terms leave cash amount, repo rate, repurchase date, margin ratio, terminability and substitution rights negotiable — the margin ratio range is deliberately very wide.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a trading currency in the CH Repo market on CO:RE?
options: CNY (Chinese yuan)
CZK (Czech koruna)
HUF (Hungarian forint)
NZD (New Zealand dollar)
questions.explanation: The supported trading currencies are AUD, CAD, CHF, CZK, DKK, EUR, GBP, HUF, JPY, NOK, NZD, PLN, SEK and USD — a far broader set than the Swiss franc alone.

questions.question: What are the business hours of the CH Repo market?
options: Business day starts at 06:00 CET, trading starts at 07:00 CET and the business day ends at 18:15 CET
24 hours a day, five days a week
questions.explanation: The market is open Monday to Friday except holidays. The window between the end of trading and 18:15 leaves room for the SNB's liquidity shortage financing facility auction.

questions.question: What is 'transaction shaping' in the CH Repo market?
options: Splitting repo transactions into tranches to limit the economic impact of settlement failures and support all-or-nothing settlement
Rounding the cash amount to the nearest million
Adjusting the repo rate to the term of the trade
Splitting a trade across several counterparties
questions.explanation: Shaping thresholds are set per currency — for example CHF, EUR, GBP and USD at 100 million, JPY at 10 billion. A failed shape blocks only one tranche instead of the whole trade.

questions.question: What is a 'currency business day' as opposed to a business day?
options: A day on which settlement in a specific currency is possible; currency holidays largely follow national public holidays
Any calendar day
A day on which the platform is open for trading
A day on which the SNB holds an auction
questions.explanation: The market can be open for trading while a currency is closed for settlement. Currency holidays follow the central bank managing that currency, which is why every currency has its own cut-off times and value days.

questions.question: Which central bank determines the currency holidays for NOK in the CH Repo market calendar?
options: Norges Bank (Central Bank of Norway)
The Swiss National Bank
The European Central Bank
Sveriges Riksbank
questions.explanation: Each trading currency maps to the central bank managing it — CHF to the SNB, EUR to the ECB, GBP to the Bank of England, NOK to Norges Bank, SEK to the Riksbank, USD to the Federal Reserve.

questions.question: Which three participation models does SIX Repo AG offer?
options: Basic, Advanced and Premium
Bronze, Silver and Gold
Standard, Professional and Institutional
Member, Sponsor and Auctioneer
questions.explanation: Each model comes with a shorter and a longer participation period, giving six pricing models in total. Higher models mean higher monthly minimum fees but reduced trading prices.

questions.question: How do the monthly minimum fee and transaction fees interact in the SIX Repo pricing model?
options: Only the difference between the minimum fee and total transaction fees is charged; once transaction fees reach the minimum, only transaction fees apply
Both are always charged in full and added together
The minimum fee replaces transaction fees entirely
The minimum fee is charged annually in advance
questions.explanation: The minimum fee acts as a floor, not a surcharge. It is shown separately on the invoice for transparency, but effectively only the shortfall is billed.

questions.question: How does trade term affect the SIX Repo transaction fee rate?
options: Rates fall as the term lengthens: short (<7 days) is most expensive per annum, long (>35 days) cheapest
Rates rise with term length
Term has no impact on the fee
Only trades above 35 days are charged at all
questions.explanation: Fees are quoted in bps per annum and applied to a term-adjusted volume, so a longer trade already pays more in absolute terms — the lower rate partly offsets that.

questions.question: Which execution type carries the LOWEST transaction fee rate in each participation model?
options: Multilateral market maker — posting a quote or RfO to the whole market
Multilateral aggressor — responding to a quote or RfO
Bilateral trading — quotes to a restricted group
All three carry identical rates
questions.explanation: Market making to the whole market is cheapest, aggressing is dearer and bilateral trading dearest. The pricing deliberately rewards visible, multilateral liquidity provision.

questions.question: Which data feeds into the Swiss reference rates, according to the SIX Repo price list?
options: Quotes and trades for multilateral market making, but only trades for aggressor and bilateral execution
All quotes on the platform regardless of execution type
Only SNB auction results
Only trades above CHF 100 million
questions.explanation: That is why the multilateral market maker category matters beyond fees: binding quotes posted to the whole market contribute to reference rate formation, which underpins SARON.

questions.question: How is an intraday trade (term under one day) treated for fee calculation?
options: A minimum term of one day is used
It is fee-free
It is charged at twice the overnight rate
It is charged a flat fee of CHF 100
questions.explanation: Without a floor, a term-adjusted fee on a sub-daily trade would round to almost nothing. The one-day minimum keeps intraday liquidity priced consistently.

questions.question: Which participants may act as auctioneer in the primary auction segment?
options: Only participants on the Advanced and Premium participation models
Every participant including Basic
Only the SNB
Only participants in a client group
questions.explanation: Being an auctioneer is a benefit of the higher models. In primary auctions the transaction fee is charged only to the auctioneer — participants bidding in the auction pay no transaction fee.

questions.question: What is a 'client group' in the SIX Repo pricing model?
options: Participants in a holding or parent-subsidiary relationship who share the monthly minimum fee and benefit from lower trading fees
Any group of participants trading with each other
A group of participants sharing one Repo Member ID
A basket of clients served by the same triparty agent
questions.explanation: The holdings must be consolidated in the group's financial statements. The minimum fee then applies to the group as a whole and is allocated pro rata to members' transaction fees.

questions.question: Which securities are traded in the secondary segment of the OTC spot market?
options: Unlisted short-term debt instruments with maturities up to one year issued by the Swiss Confederation (GMBF) or the SNB (SNB Bills)
Swiss Confederation bonds
SMI equities
Structured products
questions.explanation: Confederation bonds can be issued via primary auction but are explicitly not traded in secondary trading on SIX Repo.

questions.question: What is a GMBF (MMDRC)?
options: A short-term, usually discounted money market debt register claim issued by the Swiss Confederation
A Swiss covered bond
A money market fund managed by SIX
A collateral basket for Swiss government paper
questions.explanation: GMBF stands for Geldmarktbuchforderung der Schweizerischen Eidgenossenschaft; MMDRC (money market debt register claim) is its English equivalent. SNB Bills are the SNB's counterpart instrument.

questions.question: What are the two market segments of the OTC spot market?
options: Primary auction and secondary trading
Repo and securities lending
Listed and unlisted
Domestic and cross-border
questions.explanation: The primary segment holds auctions for new issues or issue increases and does not permit bilateral trading; the secondary segment allows bilateral trading and, for enabled participants, auctions.

questions.question: How are short-term debt instruments treated under Swiss stamp taxes?
options: Exempt from the issuance stamp duty, and instruments with maturities up to one year are exempt from turnover stamp tax, but earnings remain subject to withholding tax
Fully exempt from all Swiss taxes
Subject to issuance stamp duty but exempt from withholding tax
Subject to turnover stamp tax at the standard rate
questions.explanation: The exemption from stamp taxes is what makes very short-dated paper economic; withholding tax on the earnings still applies and has its own compliance guidance from the Federal Tax Administration and the SNB.

questions.question: Within what time must an auctioneer complete allocation and execute trades after an auction ends?
options: Within 30 minutes of the auction end time
Within 24 hours
By the end of the following business day
There is no time limit
questions.explanation: Auctions may run at any time during business hours but must not exceed one business day, and allocation must follow within 30 minutes — bidders need certainty over their funding quickly.

questions.question: What does a custodian do?
options: Holds securities in safekeeping for clients and administers them, including settlement, income collection and corporate actions
Trades securities on its own account for clients
Sets the eligibility criteria for collateral baskets
Guarantees the performance of trades it settles
questions.explanation: A custodian is a service provider to its clients. It is distinct from a CSD, which is the central book-entry layer where securities ultimately live and where final settlement occurs.

questions.question: What is a central securities depository (CSD)?
options: The institution where securities are held centrally in book-entry form and where settlement becomes final
A bank that lends securities to short sellers
The central counterparty for securities trades
A registry of legal entity identifiers
questions.explanation: SIX SIS is the Swiss CSD. Because both the securities accounts and the link to the payment system sit in one place, a CHF repo can settle delivery versus payment in central bank money in a single process.

questions.question: What does settlement mean?
options: The final transfer of securities and cash that discharges the obligations arising from a trade
The agreement of price and size between two parties
The calculation of margin requirements
The reporting of a trade to a repository
questions.explanation: Execution creates obligations; settlement extinguishes them. Finality is the point at which the transfer can no longer be unwound — which is exactly what makes DvP settlement in central bank money so valuable.

questions.question: What does clearing cover?
options: Everything between execution and settlement: confirmation, calculation of obligations, netting and risk management
The final exchange of securities against cash
The safekeeping of securities on behalf of clients
The publication of trade prices to the market
questions.explanation: Clearing establishes what is owed; settlement delivers it. Where a CCP clears, it also novates the trade and becomes counterparty to both sides.

questions.question: What is a settlement instruction?
options: The message telling a custodian or CSD what to deliver or receive, against which payment and on which date
The confirmation that a trade has been executed
The order sent to a counterparty to initiate a trade
The margin call issued after revaluation
questions.explanation: Both sides instruct separately, and the instructions must match. Mismatched or late instructions are one of the most common causes of settlement fails — and under CSDR every fail carries a daily cash penalty.

questions.question: What is netting?
options: Offsetting mutual obligations so that only the net difference is delivered or paid
Splitting a large trade into smaller tranches
Allocating collateral across several counterparties
Reducing the haircut applied to a basket
questions.explanation: Two distinct kinds matter in repo: settlement netting, which reduces the number and size of daily movements, and close-out netting, which collapses all trades into a single net claim on default. Only the latter reduces credit exposure.

questions.question: What is a corporate action?
options: An event initiated by the issuer that affects the security, such as a coupon, dividend, redemption or merger
A decision by a counterparty to terminate a repo early
A regulatory measure imposed on a listed company
An instruction to substitute collateral
questions.explanation: Corporate actions on collateral have to be handled while the security sits with someone else: income is passed back to the collateral giver as a manufactured payment, and a redemption removes the security from the pool and forces a substitution.

questions.question: What does SARON stand for?
options: Swiss Average Rate Overnight
Swiss Adjusted Reference Overnight Note
Secured Average Rate on Notes
Swiss Aggregated Repo Overnight
questions.explanation: SARON is the CHF overnight reference rate and the successor to CHF LIBOR.

questions.question: What is SARON based on?
options: Concluded transactions and binding quotes in the secured CHF interbank repo market
Survey estimates submitted by panel banks for unsecured rates
The yields of short-dated Swiss Confederation bonds
The rates of the SNB's standing facility
questions.explanation: That was the core criticism of LIBOR: estimates instead of transactions. SARON is derived from the CHF repo market, which is exactly why that market matters so much for the Swiss rates landscape.

questions.question: Which reference rate did SARON replace at the end of 2021?
options: CHF LIBOR
EURIBOR
SOFR
€STR
questions.explanation: CHF LIBOR was discontinued at the end of 2021. Earlier, in 2017, SARON had already replaced the unsecured TOIS fixing as the CHF overnight benchmark.

questions.question: Which CHF index on CO:RE is restricted to the SNB market segment?
options: The SNB Policy Rate index
SARON
€STR
TGCR
questions.explanation: SARON is available generally for variable-rate contracts, but the SNB Policy Rate index can only be referenced in contracts within the SNB market segment.

questions.question: How is SARON typically used as a term rate in loan contracts?
options: As compounded SARON in arrears — daily compounding over the interest period
As a forward-looking term rate fixed at the start of the period from panel quotes
As the arithmetic mean of policy rates over the period
As the previous year's annual average
questions.explanation: Because there is no quote-based SARON term curve, the overnight rate is compounded over the period, so the rate is only known at the end. Hence the lookback and observation shift mechanics used in contracts.

questions.question: Why does the design of a repo trading platform matter for benchmark integrity?
options: Because binding quotes and executed trades on the platform feed the calculation of the secured reference rate
Because the platform sets the benchmark itself by decree
Because benchmarks are derived from central bank auctions only
Because platform fees are added to the benchmark
questions.explanation: A transaction-based benchmark is only as robust as the data behind it. SIX's price list explicitly distinguishes which execution types contribute quotes and trades to Swiss reference rates.

questions.question: Why did moving legacy contracts from CHF LIBOR to SARON require a spread adjustment?
options: LIBOR was an unsecured term rate that embedded bank credit risk, while SARON is a secured overnight rate and therefore structurally lower
Because SARON is published in a different currency
Because SARON is calculated only once a month
Because SARON is set by the SNB rather than by the market
questions.explanation: Swapping one rate for the other without adjustment would have transferred value between borrower and lender. A fixed spread adjustment based on the historical median difference bridges the gap between an unsecured term rate and a secured overnight rate.

questions.question: What is the SIC system?
options: The Swiss interbank payment system for CHF payments in central bank money (RTGS)
The Swiss central securities depository
The trading system for Swiss equities
FINMA's reporting system for repo trades
questions.explanation: SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) is the real-time gross settlement system for the Swiss franc. It is operated on behalf of the SNB and forms the cash leg of every CHF repo settlement.

questions.question: What is the function of SIX SIS?
options: Swiss central securities depository and provider of settlement and triparty collateral management services
Trading platform for repo transactions
Central counterparty for equity trades
Operator of the SIC payment system
questions.explanation: SIX SIS maintains the securities accounts and settles transactions. As triparty agent it additionally selects, values and administers the collateral.

questions.question: What does delivery versus payment (DvP) mean?
options: Securities are only delivered if the corresponding payment is made, and vice versa
Payment is made two days after delivery
Delivery is free of payment and settled later
The buyer pays before delivery
questions.explanation: DvP links the two legs so that neither can complete without the other, eliminating principal risk. All CH Repo market and OTC spot market transactions settle on a DvP basis.

questions.question: What is the advantage of integrated settlement across SIX SIS and SIC for a CHF repo?
options: Securities and cash legs settle simultaneously and with finality in central bank money (DvP), eliminating principal risk
The trade no longer needs to be collateralised
Settlement is aggregated and processed at month end
All counterparty risk over the life of the trade is removed
questions.explanation: DvP rules out one side delivering while the other fails to pay. The running counterparty risk over the life of the repo is untouched by it — that is what haircuts and margining are for.

questions.question: Why does a repo generate two settlement events rather than one?
options: Because both the near leg and the far leg must settle, so each trade can fail twice
Because the collateral is delivered in two tranches
Because interest settles separately from principal
Because triparty always splits settlement
questions.explanation: Every repo settles at the purchase date and again at the repurchase date. This doubles the exposure to settlement discipline regimes and makes fails management particularly important in repo books.

questions.question: What is the practical effect of straight-through processing (STP) in the Swiss repo chain?
options: Trade, collateral allocation and settlement flow without manual re-entry, cutting operational risk and settlement latency
It removes the need for a master agreement
It guarantees that no trade ever fails
It allows trading outside business hours
questions.explanation: STP is what makes same-day and intraday repo viable at scale: with manual intervention, an intraday contract type settling T+0 would be impractical.

questions.question: What does the term 'Swiss Value Chain' describe?
options: The end-to-end integration of trading, settlement and payment across SIX infrastructures and the SIC system
The supply chain of the Swiss export industry
The chain of supervisory authorities over Swiss banks
A rating methodology for Swiss issuers
questions.explanation: Trading (CO:RE), custody and settlement (SIX SIS) and CHF payments (SIC) are linked, which enables true delivery versus payment in central bank money in a single process.

questions.question: Which statement about the Swiss repo market is correct?
options: It is highly standardised and runs largely electronically and triparty-based over the SIX infrastructure
It is mostly organised by telephone and bilaterally without central infrastructure
It consists almost entirely of cross-currency transactions
It is reserved exclusively for the SNB
questions.explanation: The CHF repo market is regarded as one of the most automated in the world: trading, collateral management and settlement are tightly integrated.

questions.question: Which participants are typically active on the Swiss repo platform?
options: Domestic and foreign banks, insurers, corporates with treasury operations and the SNB
Exclusively large Swiss banks
Exclusively retail investors
Exclusively central banks
questions.explanation: The platform serves a broad institutional participant base, and the SNB uses the same infrastructure for its monetary policy operations.

questions.question: What is the significance of the repo market for the implementation of Swiss monetary policy?
options: It is the central transmission channel: the SNB steers liquidity via secured operations and keeps SARON close to the policy rate
It has no practical significance for monetary policy
It only serves to refinance mortgages
It is used exclusively for foreign exchange intervention
questions.explanation: The SNB expresses its stance through the SNB policy rate and aims to keep secured money market rates, as measured by SARON, close to it.

questions.question: Which instrument does the ECB traditionally use for its main refinancing operations?
options: Reverse transactions, i.e. collateralised credit operations (repos)
Unsecured loans to banks
Direct equity purchases
FX swaps with commercial banks
questions.explanation: The Eurosystem's main refinancing operations are collateralised. Internationally, collateralisation is the norm — central banks do not extend unsecured credit.

questions.question: Why do central banks apply haircuts to collateral in their own operations?
options: To protect the public balance sheet against a fall in collateral value between default and liquidation
Because regulation forbids lending at 100% of value
To make their operations more expensive than the market
Because haircuts are required for accounting reasons
questions.explanation: The rationale mirrors the private market. Central bank haircut schedules are also policy instruments: widening the eligible set or cutting haircuts eases funding conditions in stress.

questions.question: What is TGCR, the USD index available for variable-rate contracts on CO:RE?
options: The Tri-Party General Collateral Rate, a US secured overnight rate based on triparty repo transactions
The Treasury Government Cash Rate set by the US Treasury
The Total Gross Collateral Ratio of a repo book
A US corporate bond index
questions.explanation: TGCR is one of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's secured overnight rates, alongside BGCR and SOFR, and is calculated from triparty repo activity in US Treasury collateral.

questions.question: Why does central bank eligibility of a security matter for its valuation?
options: Because it raises the security's liquidity and reduces its liquidity premium
Because the central bank guarantees its price
Because such securities are tax exempt
Because they can be excluded from the balance sheet
questions.explanation: A security that can be converted into central bank liquidity at any time is materially more valuable for treasury purposes, and this shows in its price and its repo rate.

questions.question: How does a liquidity-absorbing central bank operation affect the money market?
options: It reduces banks' sight deposits and tends to push short-term rates up
It increases sight deposits and lowers rates
It has no effect on rates
It only affects long-term capital market yields
questions.explanation: Less excess liquidity means more competition for central bank money, so secured overnight rates tend to rise towards the policy rate.

questions.question: What is tiered remuneration of sight deposits at the SNB?
options: Balances are remunerated at the policy rate up to a threshold and at a lower rate above it
All balances are remunerated uniformly at the policy rate
Only foreign banks' balances are remunerated
Remuneration depends on the bank's capital
questions.explanation: Tiering creates an incentive to lend liquidity above the threshold into the repo market rather than parking it at the central bank, which supports money market activity.

questions.question: Which statement about Swiss minimum reserve requirements is correct?
